drivers.source: Market: LightCounting AI-cluster Ethernet optics, CY2025 $16.5B (Jan 2026 forecast quoted in POET Technologies FY2025 20-F, the only cited dollar level; that edition's 2026 level $26B is not booked, sized as an alternative), CY2026-2029 levels derived by us from +120% 2026 and +76% 2027 (Lightwave 2026-10-08), CY2028 by LightCounting optics/capex ratio x Big-4 capex (Lightwave 2026-03-10; method of driver_models/CRDO/quarterly/set.json optical_tam; capex path = shared input hs_capex from NVDA's gate-clean round 2026-11-20, runs/2026-11-20/NVDA/supervisor.json row hs_capex: 1,009.45 -> 1,305.26 $B, update 2026-11-23), CY2029 +31.4% (linear fade of growth from +37.1% in 2028 to LightCounting's +20% by 2031). Wireline: KEYS does not disclose wireline dollars; Q3 FY26 prepared remarks: "Wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time this quarter" of commercial communications $1,006M (https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/transcript/Q3-FY2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf); Q3 FY26 call: wireline roughly two-thirds R&D, one-third manufacturing (Motley Fool transcript 2026-08-25). Q4 FY26 build (2026-11-18): CFO Neil Dougherty, Q3 FY26 call (src 40, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/25/keysight-keys-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/): wireline R&D/manufacturing 'more like 2/3, 1/3'; CEO Satish Dhanasekaran (src 40): Q4 mix 'even trend more toward production'; CEO (prepared remarks, src 18): wireline 'record orders, more than doubling year-over-year'; CFO (src 40): supply 'a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters'. Customers' R&D (src 56, SEC XBRL): R&D expense of the wireline customer basket (NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, COHR, LITE, ANET, CIEN, AMD) +36.0% y/y in its latest reported quarter (14,646 vs 10,773 $M); optics/network names alone +10.3%. Cross-checks: VIAVI NSE +74.1% y/y in the quarter to 2026-10-03 (src 41), of which Spirent product lines $52.7M (CFO Ilan Daskal, VIAVI Q1 FY27 call, src 54; Zacks src 55), so NSE ex Spirent +49.7% (323.4 vs 216.0); VIAVI CEO Oleg Khaykin: organic business 'grew about 50%' and data center growth 'continued robust' in calendar 2027 (src 54); hyperscaler Q3 CY26 capex Alphabet 51.4B, Microsoft 45.2B (CFO Amy Hood: Oct-Dec over $50B), Amazon 77.3B (src 50, published 2026-11-01). Market growth: LightCounting via Lightwave (src 17, published 2026-10-08). Post-print (2026-11-19): Q4 FY2026 Ex.99.1 (src 94, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104626000040/exhibit991-q426pressrelease.htm); Q4 FY26 call transcript (src 105; speakers named: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, CFO Neil Dougherty, CSG President Kailash Narayanan).
drivers.derivation: UPDATE 2026-11-23 (round 2026-11-20, shared input hs_capex): CY2028 market 87,616 and CY2029 115,151 on NVDA's gate-clean Big-4 capex path (CY2027 1,009.45 -> CY2028 1,305.26 $B, src 114; row constant:mkt), market growth +37.1% / +31.4% in 2028 / 2029; wireline FY28 +19.8% -> 3,243, FY29 +16.8% -> 3,786 (same method and elasticity); FY27 unchanged at 2,707 (CY2027 does not use the capex path). Market quarters re-interpolated, so the FY27 capture quarters move with the market's quarter shape while the FY27 wireline quarters do not. POST-PRINT 2026-11-19 (Q4 FY2026 actual, Ex.99.1 src 94; call src 105; gate round 1 fixes 2026-11-20): Q4 FY26 wireline 620 (estimate of an actual, set at the floor the CFO's words fix: CFO Neil Dougherty, Q4 FY26 call: commercial communications 1,145 'up 73%, led by triple-digit growth in wireline and robust double-digit growth in wireless', so wireline >= +100% on the Q4 FY25 310 estimate = 620; wireless is the remainder, 1,145 - 620 = 525, +50% y/y incl. Spirent, which reads as 'robust double-digit'). KEYS does not disclose wireline; the floor is the one point the call pins (the earlier 635 was CC less an assumed wireless 510, circular); 635/510 and 680/465 are sized as alternatives. Pre-print Q4 build was 566.2: the miss is the R&D/manufacturing growth (+19% q/q on Q3's 520 by our split vs +9% built) as supply let more record wireline orders ship (CFO Neil Dougherty: 'we have made now four consecutive quarters of capacity increases', src 105). FY26 1,926 (358/428/520/620). FY2027-29 method unchanged (LightCounting market path src 17/51/112; customer R&D elasticity 0.30, src 56): growth = 1/3 x market growth + 2/3 x 0.30 x market growth = +40.5% / +19.8% / +16.8% -> 2,707 / 3,243 / 3,786 (pre-print 2,631 / 3,060 / 3,502, on the older capex path). New call evidence, cross-checks only: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: AI bookings 'roughly 2.5 times' FY25 in FY26, AI customers 'nearly doubled', 1.6T 'early innings', 3.2T in R&D, CPO/NPO 'a bigger inflection in 2028'; CFO: demand 'continues to stay ahead of our ability to ship'. Within each year the quarters rise at one constant quarterly rate from the prior Q4 so the FY totals hold. Capture = wireline / market: Q4 FY26 5.47%, FY27 4.24%, FY28 3.70%, FY29 3.29%. PRE-PRINT TEXT (kept as the record): Wireline quarterly estimates (flag: not disclosed): FY25 229/257/290/310 (=1,086), FY26 Q1-Q3 358/428/520 (Q3 above wireless 486, CFO). Q4 FY26 566.2 built from what drives each part: the R&D two-thirds (346.7) grows +5.7% in the quarter (+25% a year annualised: below the customer R&D basket's +36.0% y/y in its latest quarter, src 56, and VIAVI's NSE ex Spirent +49.7%, src 41/54, so this is the conservative side) -> 366.5; the manufacturing third (173.3) grows +15.2% with transceiver units shipped (LightCounting AI-cluster optics market, quarter interpolation of the CY2026 $36.3B total: 11,333 in Aug-Oct vs 9,839 in May-Jul) -> 199.7; the production tilt the CEO describes for Q4 is the reason the manufacturing part grows faster. Supply (CFO 'governor') is why we do not convert Q3's record wireline orders (more than double y/y) faster: the build stays below order growth. FY26 1,872. FY2027-29 growth = 1/3 x market growth (manufacturing test scales with units shipped) + 2/3 x customers' lab R&D growth. R&D growth = the customers' R&D-to-market elasticity x market growth: the wireline customer basket's R&D rose +36.0% y/y (src 56) while LightCounting's CY2026 market grows +120% (src 17), elasticity 0.36/1.20 = 0.30; on the market path (+76% 2027, LightCounting src 17; +30.6% 2028 and +27.1% 2029, src 51/17) R&D grows +22.8% / +9.2% / +8.1%. Wireline FY27 +40.5% -> 2,631, FY28 +16.3% -> 3,060, FY29 +14.4% -> 3,502. Within each year the quarters rise at one constant quarterly rate from the Q4 FY26 build so the FY totals hold (wireline has no stable seasonal pattern: it is a structural ramp). Capture = wireline / market: Q4 FY26 5.00%, FY27 4.12%, FY28 3.67%, FY29 3.30%. Alternatives (judgment_alternatives): optics/network customers only (R&D elasticity 0.086), R&D at VIAVI's ex-Spirent pace, and the CY2028 market on a straight fade of LightCounting's growth.

Wireless customers' R&D (src 57, SEC XBRL): Qualcomm +17.1% y/y (quarter to 2026-06-28), Nokia +7.6% (FY2025), Ericsson -8.7% (FY2025), median +7.6%. Anritsu (direct mobile-test rival, Q2 FY2026 deck 2026-10-29, src 58): 5G smartphone development investment 'remains stagnant'; NTN, automotive and Wi-Fi 7 demand continue. Spirent (closed 2025-10-15) in the base from Q1 FY26 (10-Q Q3 FY26, src 4). Customer forward plans (2026-11-19): Qualcomm Q1 FY2027 opex guide $2.8B vs $2.45B a year earlier (CFO Akash Palkhiwala, src 81, 82); Ericsson Q3 2026 operating costs 31.4% of sales vs 34.4% (src 83, 84); Nokia cost reduction program (src 85, 86); Samsung Networks 2027 'telco investment headwinds' (src 87); MediaTek no 2027 opex statement (src 88). Spirent; CEO: wireless orders 'grew double digits'; CSG President Kailash Narayanan: 'Our 6G business doubled year-over-year'). Pre-print 495.4: +29.6 (the split is an estimate, so the miss is shared with wireline). FY26 1,841. FY2027-29 on the same four-component build from the new H2 FY26 exit (486 + 525 = 1,011 / 50.69% = 1,994.6 a year; H2 share from the Ex.99.1 end-market tables, below): Spirent-origin 225 at 0%; the rest 1,769.6 split device/chipset R&D 707.8 (40%), network R&D 530.9 (30%), manufacturing test 530.9 (30%). Rates: device/chipset R&D +5.7%/+10%/+10% (Qualcomm stated opex step x 40%, src 81, 82; 3GPP timeline src 78, 111, and CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, src 105: 'Release 21 expected in 2029', chipset and network equipment makers 'expanding from research into funded development'); network equipment R&D -1.0% in FY27 (Ericsson's cost plan x 45%, src 83-87) and 0%/0% in FY28-29 = Dell'Oro's newest RAN outlook (3Q26 release 2026-11-19, src 110; Stefan Pongratz, Vice President: 'we continue to expect a relatively flat market over the next several years'; 2027 'projected to remain broadly flat ... with a low-single-digit decline'). Vendors' R&D tracks that revenue under their cost programs. Gate round 2 (2026-11-20): the gate round 1 +1%/+1% rested on Dell'Oro's July 2026 5-year edition, which src 110 supersedes; the pre-print +4%/+4% (Rel-21 lab work, no source sizing it) is sized as an alternative; Dell'Oro's 5-year +1% CAGR editions (January and July 2026) are superseded by the 3Q26 outlook and no longer used (gate round 1 fix 2026-11-23). Manufacturing test -10% / 0% in FY27-28 (IDC, src 77: 3Q26 smartphone units -22.0% y/y, growth constrained through 2027, recovery 2028 at the earliest) and +6.3% in FY29 (gate round 2: Counterpoint Research, published 2026-08-22, src 113, Chief Analyst Wang Yang: shipments -14.3% in 2026, -1.4% in 2027, about +4.8% in 2028, and 'by the end of this decade' 6G-capable devices return the market to the 2024-2025 shipment level; on 2025 = 100 that is 85.7 / 84.5 / 88.6 to 100 in 2030 = (100 / 88.6)^(1/2) - 1 = +6.3% a year in 2029-30; FY28 stays at IDC's later 0%, Counterpoint's +4.8% and the 2029 reading +12.9% are sized as alternatives; the gate round 1 +3% had no source sizing it). PRE-PRINT TEXT (kept as the record): Q4 FY26 495.4: the 486 Q3 estimate plus one quarter of an +8% a year growth rate (+1.9% in the quarter); +8% a year is the wireless customers' R&D growth (median of Qualcomm +17.1%, Nokia +7.6%, Ericsson -8.7% = +7.6%, src 57), not a company figure: the CEO says funded 6G development programs are starting (src 18) and the CFO cites strong wireless growth (src 40), while Anritsu sees 5G smartphone development stagnant (src 58), so we take the customers' median rather than Qualcomm's pace. Orders grew significantly in Q3 and the CEO expects company orders slightly up again in Q4, but supply (CFO) gates conversion, so no backlog catch-up is added. FY26 1,811 (+29% incl. Spirent in all four quarters). FY2027-29 rebuilt ground-up 2026-11-19 (the customers'-R&D-median rate is retired for FY27-29): start from the H2 FY26 exit, Q3 486 + Q4 495.4 = 981.4, which is 50.68% of a year on the commercial communications FY23-FY25 H2 share (Ex.99.1 end-market tables, src 93, 48, 47, 46 for FY23-FY24 and src 68-71 for FY25; 50.69% on the quarter tables, gate round 1), so 1,936.5 a year; split into four components (shares are estimates: KEYS discloses neither wireless nor its R&D/manufacturing mix) and grow each on its own evidence, over the 0.75 year from the H2 FY26 midpoint to the FY27 midpoint, then full years. (1) Spirent-origin wireless 225.0 (estimate: Lifecycle Service Assurance $181.0M in 2024, -9%, plus positioning and Wi-Fi 7 test, src 79), 0% in FY27-29: operator service-assurance spend follows RAN, which Dell'Oro sees broadly flat in 2026 (src 76). (2) Device/chipset R&D 684.6 (40% of the 1,711.5 rest): FY27 +5.7% from what the customers say they will spend, weighted by an estimated share of KEYS's device test spend (KEYS does not disclose it): Qualcomm 40% (estimate, the largest merchant modem developer) at its stated step, Q1 FY2027 non-GAAP opex 'approximately $2.8 billion' (CFO and COO Akash Palkhiwala, src 81) vs the year-earlier Q1 FY2026 guide 'approximately $2.45 billion' (src 82) = +14.3%; MediaTek, Apple's modem team and other device makers 60% at 0%, because none states a 2027 R&D or opex figure (MediaTek guides only the Q4 2026 opex ratio, src 88; Apple gives none) and Qualcomm's CEO Cristiano Amon plans on handset units 'flat to down in calendar '27' (src 81): 0.40 x 14.3% = +5.7%. Qualcomm's CFO ties the opex growth to 'new skills ... as we diversify' (src 81), so some of the +14.3% is not handset R&D (alternatives below). FY28 +10% and FY29 +10% as Rel-21 specifications are written March 2027 to end-2028 toward first 6G specifications early 2029 (src 78), below Qualcomm's stated +14.3% (moderately conservative). (3) Network equipment R&D 513.5 (30%): FY27 -1.0% from the vendors' stated cost plans, weighted by an estimated share of KEYS's network test spend (Ericsson 45%, Nokia 35%, Samsung 20%; estimate from their non-China RAN positions, KEYS does not disclose it): Ericsson -2.3%, its operating costs ex restructuring at 31.4% of sales vs 34.4% a year earlier on +7% organic sales (0.314/0.344 x 1.07 - 1; src 83, 84) with cost cuts continuing (CFO Lars Sandström: 'mitigating wage pressures'; CEO Per Narvinger: 'further efficiencies over time', 2027 'could be such a transition period'); Nokia 0% (Mobile Infrastructure under a continuing 'cost reduction program', Q3 2026, src 85; the Capital Markets Day sets margin and profit targets, not an R&D figure, src 86); Samsung Networks 0% ('profitable growth ... amid telco investment headwinds' in 2027, src 87); neither states a figure, so 0% (not growing) is the upper bound of what they say: 0.45 x -2.3% = -1.0%. FY28 +4% and FY29 +4% as Rel-21 work items add lab work while Dell'Oro's newest outlook sees 'a relatively flat market over the next several years' (src 110). (4) Manufacturing test 513.5 (30%; the CFO puts wireline at 'more like 2/3, 1/3' R&D/manufacturing, src 40, and wireless 6G pre-standard work is lab-only, so a slightly smaller manufacturing share, estimate): FY27 -10% as IDC has 3Q26 smartphone shipments -22.0% y/y and growth constrained through 2027 (src 77), FY28 0% (recovery 2028 at the earliest, src 77), FY29 +3%. US budget: DoD obligated an estimated $60B of reconciliation funds from late July to 2026-09-30, ~90% of the $156B pot, and the FY2026 omnibus gave ~$860B base discretionary, the largest ever (Roll Call, published 2026-09-30, src 44); FY2027 opened on a stopgap to 2026-12-11 with no new starts and prior-year levels (ClearanceJobs, published 2026-10-01, src 45). 10-Q Q3 FY26 (src 4): ADG 339 vs 296 in Q3 (+14.5%) and 1,078 vs 908 in 9M (+18.7%), both incl. the Spirent PNT line (closed 2025-10-15). Outer years: FY2027 congressional marks match the $1.1T base discretionary request, $91B above total FY2026 enacted incl. ~$152B reconciliation, with no markup for the proposed $350B reconciliation and 'future base budgets to exceed $1 trillion' (GovExec, published 2026-08-11, src 65); after FY2027 national defense drops to $1.28T in 2028 (-14.7% nominal on the $1.5T FY2027 request) and only rises to $1.35T in 2031 (+1.8% a year) if no further reconciliation or supplemental money is approved (OMB chart via Breaking Defense, published 2026-04-03, src 117). Europe: European Allies and Canada at 2.53% of GDP in 2026 vs the Hague 3.5% core-defence target by 2035 (NATO estimates via ICDS, published 2026-07-09, src 66); CEO (src 40): 'Sovereign investments in Europe is another tailwind for our defense business'. Post-print (2026-11-19): Q4 FY2026 Ex.99.1 (src 94, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104626000040/exhibit991-q426pressrelease.htm); Q4 FY26 call transcript (src 105; speakers named: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, CFO Neil Dougherty, CSG President Kailash Narayanan).
drivers.derivation: POST-PRINT 2026-11-19 (Q4 FY2026 actual, Ex.99.1 src 94; call src 105; gate round 1 fixes 2026-11-20): Q4 FY26 ADG 351 actual (+7% reported, Ex.99.1 end-market table) vs our 379.5: organic ~+2% (7% less ~5pt Spirent PNT) vs our +10%. What was wrong: orders did not turn into revenue in the quarter; CEO Satish Dhanasekaran (src 105): ADG had 'the strongest quarter in the history of the business from a bookings point of view' and orders 'grew strong double digits', so the shortfall is conversion/timing (October CR month, supply 'heavily concentrated' in AI SKUs per the CFO), not demand. FY26 1,429. FY2027 +7.4% organic, rebuilt in gate round 1 from budgets (the pre-print +9% had no source sizing it; kept as an alternative): half US, half Europe/rest, the split used for FY28-29 (KEYS does not split ADG by region; the CEO says growth is across all regions). US part +9.0%: the FY2027 congressional marks sign off on the $1.1 trillion discretionary request, '$91 billion more than the total FY26 enacted level', which included ~$152B of reconciliation (GovExec / Forecast International, 2026-08-11, src 65): 91 / (1,100 - 91) = +9.0% nominal. Europe part +5.8% (NATO Europe/Canada 2.53% of GDP in 2026 to 3.5% by 2035, +3.7%/yr, plus 2% inflation, src 66). 0.5 x 9.0% + 0.5 x 5.8% = +7.4% -> 1,534.7. Not added on top: record Q4 ADG bookings into backlog (src 105) against the CR to 2026-12-11 that delays Q1 new starts (src 45); sized as the +12% and +3% alternatives. FY2028 +2.9% -> 1,579.3, FY2029 +3.9% -> 1,640.8 (half US / half Europe, src 65, 66, 117). Quarters by the FY23-FY25 mean ADG quarter shares 25.19/24.40/24.13/26.28% (Ex.99.1 end-market tables: FY23 310/310/307/323 and FY24 295/277/275/303, src 93, 48, 47, 46; FY25 311/301/296/330, src 68-71). PRE-PRINT TEXT (kept as the record): Q4 FY26 379.5 built y/y on the same quarter's actual (330, Q4 FY25): organic +10% (CEO: ADG orders up double digits in all regions and backlog built in Q3; the DoD obligated ~$60B of reconciliation money in Aug-Sep on top of a record base budget, which reaches the primes and labs that buy KEYS test gear; the October CR month limits new starts, so organic growth stays at the low end of double-digit orders) plus +5pt from Spirent's PNT line, which was in the base for only two weeks of Q4 FY25 (closed 2025-10-15, 10-Q src 4). The 10-Q's acquisition points by end market were not readable at the gate; the closest disclosed figure is CSG revenue +43% reported vs +36% core in Q3 FY26 (CFO Neil Dougherty, Q3 FY26 call, src 40; core excludes acquisitions of the last 12 months and currency), a 7pt gap; in Q4 FY26 Spirent is unanniversaried for ~10 of 13 weeks (anniversary 2025-10-15), so 7pt x 10/13 = ~5pt (labelled estimate, confidence medium). FY26 1,458. FY2027 +9% (organic; the CR to 2026-12-11 delays new starts in Q1, while the FY2026 record budget and the reconciliation obligations made in Aug-Sep convert to orders through FY27; Europe sovereign spending per CEO, src 40) -> 1,589; FY2028 +2.9% -> 1,635, FY2029 +3.9% -> 1,698: half US, half Europe/rest (judgment: KEYS does not split ADG by region; the CEO says growth is across all regions, src 18). US part: FY2028 flat in nominal terms (base discretionary held near the $1.1T FY2027 level while reconciliation money ends, src 65, 117), FY2029 +2% (inflation at the Fed's 2% target; the OMB chart's $1.28T 2028 -> $1.35T 2031 is +1.8% a year, src 117). Europe part: +5.8% a year = the share path from 2.53% of GDP (2026) to 3.5% by 2035 (+3.7% a year, src 66) plus 2% inflation (ECB target). 0.5 x 0% + 0.5 x 5.8% = 2.9% (FY28); 0.5 x 2% + 0.5 x 5.8% = 3.9% (FY29). Quarters by the mean ADG quarter share of FY23-FY25 (25.2/24.4/24.1/26.3%; Ex.99.1 end-market tables src 93, 48, 47, 46 and 68-71). Alternatives: a full-year CR holds FY27 near +3%; a reconciliation-led year +12%; FY28-29 US-led (0% / +2%) or Europe-led (+5.8% / +5.8%).

CFO Neil Dougherty (Q3 FY26 call, src 40): total revenue +36% reported / +31% core and CSG +43% / +36% core, so acquisitions and currency explain ~5pt of total growth (~$68M on 1,352) and ~7pt of CSG (~$66M on 940), leaving ~$2M (~0.5pt) for EISG (rounding of the percentages allows about -$20M to +$25M; labelled estimate, confidence low). Peers for the Aug-Oct window: Teradyne Q3 2026 revenue 1,306 (Q2 1,329) and Q4 guide 1,250-1,350 (src 42, published 2026-10-27); Advantest Apr-Sep 2026 Test System sales +61.2% (src 43, published 2026-10-28). Outer years: SEMI mid-year forecast (published 2026-07-14, src 63): test equipment $15.3B in 2026 (+31.0%) and $20.8B in 2028 = +16.6% a year 2026-28; IMF WEO October 2026 (src 67): global growth 3.4% in 2027. Post-print (2026-11-19): Q4 FY2026 Ex.99.1 (src 94, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104626000040/exhibit991-q426pressrelease.htm); Q4 FY26 call transcript (src 105; speakers named: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, CFO Neil Dougherty, CSG President Kailash Narayanan).

What was wrong: the organic growth rate (we eased it from Q3's ~+21% to ~+18.5%; it eased to ~+15%); orders were not the issue (CEO, src 105: Q4 orders 'up significantly in each of our three markets', semiconductor orders double digits, automotive back to growth). FY26 1,961. FY2027 +10% (record EISG orders, SEMI test +16.6%/yr 2026-28, src 63) -> 2,157.1; FY2028 +7.6% (semiconductor test about a third of EISG at SEMI's test-equipment path, the rest at IMF global real growth: 0.32 x 16.6% + 0.68 x 3.4% = 5.3 + 2.3 = 7.6%, src 63/67; gate round 2, 2026-11-20: the earlier booking of 7%, a 0.6pt cut with no source, is dropped and the stated mapping booked) -> 2,321.0; FY2029 +6% -> 2,460.3: no outside forecast for EISG's markets reaches 2029 (SEMI's mid-year forecast stops at 2028, src 63; IMF WEO at 2027, src 67; searched again 2026-11-20: 360iResearch's general-purpose electronic test and measurement forecast, 7.96% a year 2026-32, is dated 2026-03-23, past the 120-day window, cross-check only). +6% sits between the two outside-forecast builds for FY29, IMF-only real growth +3.4% (semis test flat after SEMI's 2028 record) and the FY28 SEMI/IMF mapping carried a year +7.6%; KEYS's 2023 whole-company 5-7% organic model (src 107) is a cross-check only, not a guide for EISG. Both FY29 options move the target under 0.5% (engine-sized), so the year is noted, not carded (rule 26, small_flag_notes). Quarters by the FY23-FY25 mean electronic industrial quarter shares 25.65/24.47/24.93/24.94% (Ex.99.1 end-market tables: FY23 442/453/464/420 and FY24 420/376/370/393, src 93, 48, 47, 46; FY25 415/393/412/429, src 68-71; FY24 is a downcycle year but kept so the shape has three years). PRE-PRINT TEXT (kept as the record): Q4 FY26 510.5 built y/y on the same quarter's actual (429, Q4 FY25): +19.0% y/y = organic ~+18.5% (Q3 EISG +21.6% reported, 501 / 412 in the Ex.99.1 and 10-Q segment tables, src 2 and 4, which the CFO rounds to 'an increase of 21%', src 40; less ~0.5pt acquisitions, estimate from the CFO's total and CSG reported-vs-core gaps, src 40, so Q3 organic ~+21%; double-digit orders in all three markets support it; Teradyne guides Oct-Dec flat with Jul-Sep at the midpoint, so semis test is plateauing at a high level and organic growth eases) plus ~+0.5pt from acquisitions (same estimate). The total is unchanged from the earlier split (organic +15% + 4pt acquisitions), which rested on a 10-Q acquisition figure the gate could not confirm; on the remaining evidence organic growth eases ~2.5pt from Q3's ~+21% to ~+18.5%. FY26 1,974. FY2027 +10% (EISG record orders with 'meaningful double-digit order growth across all three markets', CEO src 18; semis test +16.6% a year 2026-28 per SEMI, src 63; slowing from Q4's ~+18.5% organic as semis test plateaus per Teradyne's flat Q4 guide), FY2028 +7%: semiconductor test is about a third of EISG (TER-matched share 0.08 of company revenue / EISG 0.25, comps_summary fit; estimate) growing with SEMI's test equipment path (+16.6%) and the other two-thirds (automotive & energy, general electronics) with global real growth (IMF 3.4%, src 67): 0.32 x 16.6% + 0.68 x 3.4% = 7.6%, booked 7% (conservative side). FY2029 +6%: no outside forecast reaches 2029 (SEMI stops at 2028, IMF at 2027): open judgment, alternatives below. Quarters by the mean EISG quarter share of FY23-FY25 (25.7/24.5/24.9/24.9%; Ex.99.1 end-market tables src 93, 48, 47, 46 and 68-71; FY24 is a downcycle year but kept so the shape has three years). CFO Neil Dougherty, Q3 FY26 prepared remarks (src 18): CSG gross margin 70.8%, op margin 34.0%; core 'operating margin incremental of 66 percent'; synergy realization 'will accelerate in Q4', 80-90% of the $100M run-rate exiting FY26. CFO on the call (src 40): FY27 'outperform our 40% leverage target, particularly given the synergy realization'; ~$40M realized in FY26, ~$50M more FY26 to FY27; 'upper 60s percent' gross margin sustainable; one-time tariff gains 'won't repeat'. CEO (src 40): Q4 mix toward production. Peer: VIAVI non-GAAP op margin 29.0% (Ex.99.1, src 41); CFO Ilan Daskal guides 29.3% +/- 30bp for Oct-Dec (VIAVI call, src 54; Zacks src 55). CFO (src 40): FY26 synergies 'close to $40 million', FY26 to FY27 'on the order of $50 million', 'close to 90% of that $100 million realized as we enter next fiscal year'. Segment record (2026-11-20): Ex.99.1 segment tables FY23-FY26 (src 89-94, 46-48, 68-71, 24, 3, 2); core growth, core margin, acquisition points and IEEPA amounts: CFO Neil Dougherty, Q1/Q2 FY26 prepared remarks (src 95, 96) and Q3 (src 18). Post-print (2026-11-19): Q4 FY2026 Ex.99.1 (src 94, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104626000040/exhibit991-q426pressrelease.htm); Q4 FY26 call transcript (src 105; speakers named: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, CFO Neil Dougherty, CSG President Kailash Narayanan).

POST-PRINT 2026-11-19 (Q4 FY2026 actual, Ex.99.1 src 94; call src 105; gate round 1 fixes 2026-11-20): Q4 FY26 CSG 37.1% actual (555 / 1,496; gross margin 70.6%, CFO) vs our 35.9%: the miss is the incremental, 57.5% reported (61.0% organic) vs our 56.8% on a smaller revenue step, plus higher revenue (1,496 vs 1,441). FY2027-29 re-based on the ACTUAL Q4 exit (Kilian 2026-11-20): Q4 x 4 = 2,220 op income on 5,984 revenue (37.1%). Segment record incl. Q4: CSG y/y incrementals (Ex.99.1 segment tables, src 89-94, 46-48, 68-71, 24, 3, 2) FY23 14.4% on -3.1%, FY24 55.5% decremental on -7.2%, FY25 21.2% on +8.9%; quarters Q1 FY23 52% ... Q4 FY25 16%, Q4 FY26 57.5% reported. Organic FY26 (acquisitions and IEEPA out; our estimates, not figures the CFO states): Q1 42.2%, Q2 54.0%, Q3 63.1% = y/y change in CSG income from operations over the change in revenue (Ex.99.1 segment tables) after stripping the acquired revenue, reported less CSG core growth (CFO Neil Dougherty, prepared remarks: CSG 'up 16 percent on a core basis' Q1, 'up 27 percent on a core basis' Q2, 'up 36 percent on a core basis' Q3, src 95, 96, 18; acquired 99.7 / 105.5 / 66.6) at the company non-core margin (reported less core operating income: Q1 9.4% from the CFO's 28.9% core margin on core growth +14%, Q3 -2.1% from 34.7% on +31%, Q2 the mean), and the Q2 IEEPA refund out (CSG +38 op income / -34 revenue; src 96, 3); Q4 61.0% (CSG core +45%, CFO src 105: organic revenue 990 x 1.45 = 1,435.5; acquired/FX revenue 60.5 at the acquisitions' Q4 operating margin 32%, CFO src 105, = 19.4; organic op income 535.6 vs 264); full year 57.8% on +31.4% organic. Build: the line through the segment's up-years (+8.9%, 21.2%) and (+31.4%, 57.8%), slope 1.63pt per point of growth, intercept 6.7%, capped at gross margin 70.6% less ~12% variable opex = 58.6%: FY27 CSG growth +19.7% -> 38.8%, FY28 +10.5% -> 23.8%, FY29 +10.4% -> 23.7%. No synergy step: CFO (src 105) 'on a run rate basis, we have now realized the full $100 million of cost synergies' (the pre-print ~$30M FY27 / ~$10M FY28 steps are in the Q4 exit); his 'incremental margin improvement for these businesses in fiscal 2027' is unquantified (sized as an alternative, +0.6%). IEEPA: the Q4 FY26 Ex.99.1 names no IEEPA refund (src 94; the Q2 FY26 refund, +$38M CSG / +$19M EISG per the 10-Q, is the one stripped from the FY26 organic points), the CFO calls FY26's 110bp gross-margin tailwind 'one-time' (src 105) and the CEO says the record exit gross margin came 'even accounting for the 100 basis points or so impact from tariffs' (src 105); no filing or call states a Q4 refund amount, so none is stripped from the Q4 exit (the $64M of claims outstanding at 2026-07-31, 10-Q src 4, sits in adjustments). Result 37.2% FY27, 35.9% FY28, 34.7% FY29 (pre-print 36.1/35.1/33.9). The pre-print '66% core incrementals' pick is superseded. Cross-checks only, never applied: CFO FY27 company leverage 'mid to upper 40s' and FY26 ~50% ex acquisitions/IEEPA (src 105). Quarters within each year: op income = year margin x average quarterly revenue + that year's incremental x the quarter's deviation from the average.

US budget: DoD obligated an estimated $60B of reconciliation funds from late July to 2026-09-30, ~90% of the $156B pot, and the FY2026 omnibus gave ~$860B base discretionary, the largest ever (Roll Call, published 2026-09-30, src 44); FY2027 opened on a stopgap to 2026-12-11 with no new starts and prior-year levels (ClearanceJobs, published 2026-10-01, src 45). 10-Q Q3 FY26 (src 4): ADG 339 vs 296 in Q3 (+14.5%) and 1,078 vs 908 in 9M (+18.7%), both incl. the Spirent PNT line (closed 2025-10-15). Outer years: FY2027 congressional marks match the $1.1T base discretionary request, $91B above total FY2026 enacted incl. ~$152B reconciliation, with no markup for the proposed $350B reconciliation and 'future base budgets to exceed $1 trillion' (GovExec, published 2026-08-11, src 65); after FY2027 national defense drops to $1.28T in 2028 (-14.7% nominal on the $1.5T FY2027 request) and only rises to $1.35T in 2031 (+1.8% a year) if no further reconciliation or supplemental money is approved (OMB chart via Breaking Defense, published 2026-04-03, src 117). Europe: European Allies and Canada at 2.53% of GDP in 2026 vs the Hague 3.5% core-defence target by 2035 (NATO estimates via ICDS, published 2026-07-09, src 66); CEO (src 40): 'Sovereign investments in Europe is another tailwind for our defense business'. Advantest and Anritsu are still missing: they are not in the US IBES/CRSP panel and the Tokyo price history is not in the data plan this round, so the median is kept. Booked P/E 20.44x ex-SBC (SOTP 22.65x costed with the ADG peers rebuilt on Teledyne and Curtiss-Wright 2026-11-23, both on ex-amortization EPS, k=0.8, x0.911 SBC, x0.957 growth term re-run 2026-11-23 on the hs_capex-updated set). Sizes on base 367.89 (round 2026-11-20 set after the 2026-11-23 hs_capex and non-operating line update, the gate round 1 fixes, the ADG peer fix and the gate round 3 Curtiss-Wright basis fix).

options.label: No compression: peer-set median (booked)
options.reasoning: KEYS and three T&M peers traded at a median +0.25% to their own through-cycle forward P/E at their margin peaks; expansion not credited, so 0.0% on both legs.

options.label: KEYS own peak gap -0.6%
options.reasoning: KEYS's own forward P/E in FY2023, its margin-peak year, vs its 2015-25 median, on both legs.

options.label: KEYS on the src 97 windows -4.2%
options.reasoning: The FY2022-23 peak vs a 2018-24 median on IBES; the shorter base window lifts the median and creates the gap.

options.label: NI peak -25.5%
options.reasoning: The one peer that compressed: NI's forward P/E in CY2010 vs its 2000-23 median, which early-2000s multiples inflate; its CY2020 near-peak was -1.5%.

options.label: Teradyne peak +33.6%
options.reasoning: Teradyne's forward P/E at its CY2021 peak vs its 2000-25 median: the market paid more at the peak. Not booked (no expansion credited).

options.label: No growth term
options.reasoning: Zacks FY2028 consensus rests on one estimate (Nasdaq response 2026-11-20), so the 0.957 growth factor is dropped on both legs.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: Across KEYS and the three peers with point-in-time data the margin-peak gap centers near zero (two near 0, one +34%, one -26%), so a compression is not in the evidence; the downside case keeps the trough multiple.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Which optics-market path should drive wireline test revenue FY2027-29?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: wl_capture turns the LightCounting AI-cluster optics market into KEYS wireline revenue: 1/3 manufacturing with optics units + 2/3 R&D growing at an elasticity 0.30 to market growth (customer R&D basket +36.0% y/y vs LightCounting CY2026 +120%, src 56/17). Post-print the base is FY26 wireline 1,926 with Q4 at 620, the floor of CFO Neil Dougherty's wireline 'triple-digit growth' (+100% on the 310 Q4 FY25 estimate; wireless the remainder 525, +50%, 'robust double-digit'; KEYS does not disclose wireline dollars, src 105), so FY27-29 are 2,707 / 3,243 / 3,786 with the CY2028-29 market on NVDA's 2026-11-20 Big-4 capex path (src 114; 2026-11-23 update). CEO: AI bookings ~2.5x FY25 in FY26 and customers nearly doubled (src 105), cross-checks only. The market edition and R&D pace are the call. Sizes on base 367.89 (round 2026-11-20 set after the 2026-11-23 hs_capex and non-operating line update, the gate round 1 fixes, the ADG peer fix and the gate round 3 Curtiss-Wright basis fix).

options.label: Booked: LightCounting Oct-2026 path, 0.30 elasticity
options.reasoning: LightCounting's October 2026 edition (+120% 2026, +76% 2027) and the measured customer R&D elasticity from SEC XBRL; the newest dated forecast.

options.label: CY2026 at the January 2026 edition $26.0B
options.reasoning: LightCounting's older January 2026 level (POET 20-F) with the booked growth after it, which lifts the R&D elasticity to 0.625 and wireline growth.

options.label: VIAVI NSE ex Spirent pace (R&D +40/+20/+10%)
options.reasoning: VIAVI's NSE grew +49.7% y/y ex Spirent in Jul-Sep 2026 (CEO Oleg Khaykin: organic ~+50%); lab R&D at that pace.

options.label: Straight fade of market growth
options.reasoning: CY2028-29 market growth fades linearly from +76% to LightCounting's +20% by 2031 (+62%, +48%), above the booked capex-ratio path.

options.label: Bumpy Ride: flat CY2028
options.reasoning: LightCounting October 2026 edition's 'bumpy-ride' scenario, a supply-chain correction during 2027-2030 (IEEE ComSoc summary, src 112), with no year levels; our sizing: CY2028 flat, CY2029 +20%.

options.label: Optics/network customers only (elasticity 0.086)
options.reasoning: Only the optics and network customers' R&D (+10.3% y/y) sets the pace, so lab R&D grows far slower than the market.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It uses the newest dated market forecast and the measured customer R&D elasticity; the options bracket it from both sides, and the Q4 split (620-680, with 635 the previous booking) moves the target under 0.3%.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Should EISG revenue follow the booked FY27-29 path or an FY24-type downturn?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: ei_rev is Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue (semiconductor, general electronics, automotive and energy). Q4 FY26 printed 498 (+16%; pre-print 510.5), FY26 1,961. Booked FY27 +10%, FY28 +7.6% (0.32 x SEMI test +16.6% + 0.68 x IMF 3.4% = 7.6%; gate round 2 booked the stated mapping, dropping an unsourced 0.6pt cut), FY29 +6%: 2,157 / 2,321 / 2,460. FY29 alone (IMF-only +3.4% or the FY28 mapping +7.6%) moves the target under 0.5% (-0.03% / +0.02%), so it is noted, not on this card (rule 26). CEO (src 105): EISG Q4 orders 'up significantly in each of our three markets' and automotive back to growth. The FY24-type downturn (EISG -12%, src 46) moves the target more than 5%, so it is carded. Sizes on base 367.89 (round 2026-11-20 set after the 2026-11-23 hs_capex and non-operating line update, the gate round 1 fixes, the ADG peer fix and the gate round 3 Curtiss-Wright basis fix).

options.label: Booked: +10% / +7.6% / +6%
options.reasoning: Semis test demand (SEMI test equipment forecast) and global growth (IMF) mapped by EISG's end-market mix, with Q4 orders up in all three markets.

options.label: FY24-type downturn: -12%, then +5%/+5%
options.reasoning: EISG fell 12% in FY24 as industrial/auto and semis test turned; a repeat in FY27.

options.label: Semis boom continues: FY27 +15%
options.reasoning: Advantest Test System +61% Apr-Sep 2026 and EISG orders up significantly: the semis test boom carries EISG higher in FY27.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It follows the dated SEMI and IMF forecasts by end market; the FY24 repeat is a downside case, not the base, with Q4 FY26 EISG orders up significantly in all three markets (CEO, src 105).

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Which 6G R&D path should build wireless test revenue in FY2028-29?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: wireless_rev is KEYS's wireless test revenue (commercial communications less our wireline estimate; KEYS does not disclose it), built from the H2 FY26 exit (Q3 486 + Q4 525 = 1,011 / 50.69% = 1,994.6 a year) in four components: Spirent-origin 225 at 0%, device/chipset R&D 40%, network-equipment R&D 30%, manufacturing test 30% (shares are estimates). FY27 rests on customers' stated plans (Qualcomm's Q1 FY2027 opex step +14.3% x 40% = +5.7%, src 81, 82; Ericsson's cost cut x 45% = -1.0%, src 83-87; IDC handsets, src 77). The gate (round 2) found FY28-29 unsourced: device/chipset R&D +10%/+10% rests on the 3GPP timeline only (Rel-21 specifications March 2027 to end-2028, first 6G specifications early 2029, Ericsson src 78; CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: customers 'expanding from research into funded development', src 105), and no source sizes the level; a search on 2026-11-20 (6G R&D spend forecasts, chipset vendors' R&D plans) found none (ABI Research's 6G outlook gives 6G radio revenue, not R&D; MediaTek's $5B plan is AI data-center chips). The FY29 manufacturing-test step is now sourced: Counterpoint Research (2026-08-22, src 113) sees shipments -1.4% in 2027, about +4.8% in 2028 and back to the 2024-25 level by the end of the decade, which gives +6.3% a year in 2029-30 (booked; was +3% unsourced). Network R&D FY28-29 0% on Dell'Oro's 3Q26 outlook 'a relatively flat market over the next several years' (src 110). Booked FY27-29 1,980.2 / 2,054.0 / 2,166.0. Every option moves the target under 1%, but the same-period range (-0.37% to +0.71%) is above the 0.5% line, so the row is carded (rules 4, 24, 26). Sizes on base 367.89 (round 2026-11-20 set after the 2026-11-23 hs_capex and non-operating line update, the gate round 1 fixes, the ADG peer fix and the gate round 3 Curtiss-Wright basis fix).

options.label: Booked: device R&D +10%/+10%, FY29 handsets +6.3%
options.reasoning: Device/chipset R&D grows +10% a year while Rel-21 specifications are written toward the first 6G specifications in early 2029 (below Qualcomm's stated +14.3% opex step, moderately conservative); network R&D flat with Dell'Oro's RAN outlook; manufacturing test follows Counterpoint's handset recovery in FY29.

options.label: Faster 6G: device R&D +14.3%, network R&D +7.6%
options.reasoning: Device/chipset R&D at Qualcomm's stated opex step (+14.3%, Q1 FY2027 $2.8B vs $2.45B) and network R&D at Nokia's last reported R&D growth (+7.6% FY2025, SEC XBRL) in FY28-29, as 6G moves from studies to funded development.

options.label: Slower 6G: device R&D +5% in FY28-29
options.reasoning: Rel-21 slips and device/chipset R&D grows near the FY27 customer-weighted pace (+5% a year) while handset units only recover in 2028 (IDC); network R&D stays flat with Dell'Oro's 'relatively flat market over the next several years'.

options.label: FY29 handsets at the 2024-25 level in 2029 (+12.9%)
options.reasoning: Reads Counterpoint's 'by the end of this decade' as 2029, so FY29 manufacturing test jumps +12.9% (100 / 88.6) instead of +6.3% a year over 2029-30; device R&D as booked.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It sits between Qualcomm's stated step and the FY27 customer-weighted pace, on the dated 3GPP timeline, with the handset step now on Counterpoint's forecast; no option moves the target more than 0.71%.
